property_summary: updateDelay always reverts unless called by the timelock contract itself, and the minimum delay is unchanged afterwards.
A timelock admin who grants itself the proposer role can schedule an operation (timestamp = block.timestamp + delay when delay >= minDelay) and then cancel it, which erases the operation's timestamp.
An address without the proposer role cannot schedule an operation: schedule reverts and no operation with the derived id exists afterwards.
renounceRole reverts when the specified account is not the caller, and afterwards the account still holds exactly the same roles.
After successfully scheduling an operation with delay d, the operation is pending with timestamp block.timestamp + d and is not yet ready or done, for any parameters.
Cancelling an operation that is not pending must revert, for any id.
granting a role reverts unless the caller holds that role's admin role, and the role is not granted.
updateDelay reverts unless called by the timelock itself, and the minimum delay is unchanged afterwards.
The admin role of every timelock role (TIMELOCK_ADMIN, PROPOSER, EXECUTOR) is TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, for any input.
Scheduling an operation sets its timestamp to exactly block.timestamp + delay, and the delay must be at least the minimum delay.

property_summary: Cancelling a pending operation deletes its timestamp so it is no longer an operation.
A call to schedule by an address without the PROPOSER_ROLE always reverts and leaves no operation scheduled.
Granting a role by an account holding the role's admin role (TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE) makes hasRole(role, account) true.
After a proposer schedules an operation with a positive delay, the operation is pending, is an operation, and is not yet ready.

For any fresh operation scheduled by a proposer with delay >= getMinDelay(), getTimestamp(id) becomes block.timestamp + delay and equals block.timestamp + delay thereafter (and the operation is pending when delay >= 1).
After a proposer schedules an operation with sufficient delay, cancelling it resets getTimestamp(id) to 0 and makes the operation no longer pending.
Once an address no longer holds TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, any attempt by it to grant PROPOSER_ROLE reverts and the target still does not have the role.
renounceRole for an account other than msg.sender always reverts and leaves role membership unchanged.
After being granted an arbitrary role and then renouncing it for itself, msg.sender no longer holds that role (renounce-for-self succeeds).
hashOperation of a single target matches hashOperationBatch over a one-element batch with identical parameters.
After being granted PROPOSER_ROLE, scheduling an operation with delay >= minDelay records its timestamp as exactly block.timestamp + delay under its operation hash.
